text: **3. There's no "why now," and it's a hole.** "A tool built for one person fits that person perfectly" has been true since the first program was written. It wasn't *actionable* because building was expensive — that's Lancaster's whole point, variety loses to scale economics. Your draft never says what changed. And here's the thing: the research honestly reports that "AI made software cheap" is still a hypothesis with mixed evidence (METR found 19% *slower*, then couldn't get a clean read). You have something the studies don't: you went and built the things. n=1, but it's direct evidence for the only claim your essay needs — not that it's cheap for everyone, but that the threshold has moved far enough that one person can now sit on their own ideal point. Claim exactly that much and no more. It's more credible than the strong version. [...] 5. Why this is possible now and wasn't before. Bounded claim.
